title: Hydromorphodynamic Impacts Extend Beyond the Recirculation Zone of a Spur Dike on a Mobile Bed
content:
Abstract

Spur dikes generate a recirculation zone, and reattachment length is used to estimate hydraulic effects and guide structure spacing. Fixed-bed studies of non-submerged, impermeable spur dikes commonly report primary recirculation lengths on the order of 10 dike lengths, but direct measurements over deformed mobile beds remain sparse. We test whether the end of the recirculation region also marks the end of the downstream flow and bed response. We analyze a 32-day clear-water mobile-bed flume experiment with post-run three-component velocity measurements and a final bed survey. Across two elevations and two criteria, estimates of the primary reverse-flow extent span 1.00–2.68 dike lengths. At the same measured locations in each included section, the difference from the upstream velocity field reached a local minimum at eight dike lengths, then increased, with later values above the comparison level through 16 dike lengths. The farther downstream reach contained an oblique depositional macroform and about 96% of the mapped deposition. At the final velocity section, 20 dike lengths downstream, the streamwise momentum-flux centroid on the common coordinates was displaced toward the structure side, having reversed between 12 and 16 dike lengths, while the lower part of the flow still showed momentum deficit, elevated turbulence, and secondary circulation. Structure-side bed deformation extended to the survey limit at 24 dike lengths. In this experiment, the primary recirculation region was therefore short relative to the longer reach of altered flow and bed topography. Reattachment length alone did not describe the full downstream response of the mobile-bed channel.
